title: Distrust Toward The Nation
paragraphs: “They’re trying to make us kill Naofumi… It’s like something out of a novel I’ve read online.”
Itsuki nodded subtly in agreement.
Does he have some kind of compulsion to link everything back to knowledge from his original world?
“A novel? What’s that?”
“It’s a type of story. There are tales where someone is summoned to another world but is abandoned by the kingdom or summoners because they don’t like them, only to rise to greatness later.”
“Oh…”
“It also feels like a scenario you’d find in a video game story.”
“Now that you mention it, I remember a friend telling me about a beta test for a game with a story like that.”
“This is neither a novel nor a game.”
“So, you’re saying Naofumi is at the brink of experiencing something like that? By the way, in the original timeline—where we didn’t know the truth—what did we do next?”
Itsuki asked with great interest.
Should I really tell him? It wasn’t exactly a pleasant future. However, Father had told me that I should explain everything without hiding anything.

“First, in the original timeline… I knew nothing. That woman—no, from now on, I’ll just call her ‘the crimson swine’ because of her hair color—fooled me, and I ended up falsely accusing Naofumi of being a rapist.”
“If someone acted like a victim and put on fake tears, I can see how we might have believed it and looked down on Naofumi.”
“A false accusation of rape… That reminds me, one of the women in my party was rather blatant with her attempts to seduce me. I must admit, I got a little carried away.”
Ren and Itsuki nodded several times. It seemed they found my story plausible based on their own experiences.
“Naofumi—ugh, this is getting tedious. I’ll just say it outright. In the future, I came to respect and admire Naofumi as Father.”
“What!?”
“That conversation took a bizarre turn out of nowhere!”
Oh? Did I say something strange? Ah, right. Father had taught me how to handle situations like this.
“I’ll explain how that happened as well. While we were each leveling up and completing quests for the kingdom, Father received no support at all.”
“…I figured as much.”
“I mean, even if it was a false accusation, he was still branded as a rapist.”
“They summoned him against his will and then treated him like that? What a bunch of selfish bastards.”
“Unforgivable.”
Thanks to the evidence I had shown them, Ren and Itsuki were willing to listen. As expected, gaining their trust had to be done in stages.
“After overcoming the first Wave, Father used the aid money—what little he was given—to buy a filolial… Filo-tan, to be precise.”
“Ah, that bird, right? And then?”
“When raised by a Hero, filolials undergo a special kind of growth. They transform into angelic beings.”
“Haa…”
“At a time when I was at my lowest, Filo-tan comforted me. That’s when I fell in love with her from the bottom of my heart.”
“…So, because Naofumi is the one who raised Filo, you started calling him ‘Father’ out of admiration?”
“Exactly.”
“If I hadn’t witnessed today’s events, I wouldn’t believe a single word of this. Honestly, I’m still only half-convinced.”

It was proving difficult to make Ren and Itsuki fully believe me. However, it seemed like they were starting to trust me, even if just a little. For them to believe me at all—it almost felt like I was dreaming.
“Later, I shall demonstrate the growth of a Filolial myself.”
“Get back to the point. What happened to us after that?”
Ren pressed for an answer, sounding almost interrogative. It seemed he was eager to learn about the future.
“First of all, because we did as we pleased all over the land, the ecosystem of the monsters in the kingdom changed, which caused problems.”
“Don’t they just respawn?”
“Monsters are living creatures too. If you kill them, their numbers decrease.”
“…W-well, yeah. That makes sense. And then?”

“On top of that, we left many guild jobs half-finished, which ended up causing even more disasters. In my case, I used my game knowledge to unseal a certain type of plant, thinking it would help a village suffering from famine. However, the plant went berserk and turned into a massive catastrophe.”

In the game’s quest, that would have been a proper solution. But based on my previous loop, that plant most likely went out of control. Later, I heard that Father was the one who dealt with it. I explained all of this from top to bottom.
“That applies to both me and Itsuki too?”
“Yes, exactly.”
Oh? Should I also talk about the rivals and sidekicks? Or is Itsuki the bigger issue here?
“According to Father, Itsuki played the role of a ‘deputy commander’—like in those historical dramas—trying to act righteously but failing miserably.”
“Itsuki, did you have plans for something like that?”
“W-well… it was just a quest. Ren, haven’t you done similar things in games before?”
“Yeah… I’ve taken on well-rewarded quests like that before.”
“But in the end, you were just being used by the kingdom. Well, in the original world, I was also complicit in similar acts, so I can’t say much.”
In fact, in the original world, I was the one leading those efforts. Compared to me, Itsuki’s situation wasn’t as bad.

“Because of our selfish actions, the country’s dominant religion, the Church of the Three Heroes, eventually came to despise us. Meanwhile, Father cleaned up our messes and gained the trust of the people.”
“So while we were doing as we pleased, Naofumi, who was falsely accused and had to start from the bottom, ended up standing out in contrast.”
“That paints an unpleasant future where we end up being treated as villains…”
Well, I can understand Itsuki’s frustration. Thinking about my own past misdeeds also made my chest tighten.
“But… it’s not an entirely unrealistic outcome. Then what?”

“Eventually, the Church of the Three Heroes plotted to eliminate all the Heroes. They spread the lie that Father had kidnapped the younger sister of the crimson swine. I chased after him, but when Ren and Itsuki started to realize the truth, they were caught in a trap.”
“Wait… don’t tell me we get killed at that point!?”
“No? Fortunately, you manage to survive the crisis, and in the end, the true masterminds—the Church of the Three Heroes—are defeated.”
“Wait a second. What happens to the king and princess?”

“That man is not a true king. This country follows a matriarchal monarchy, and the queen was away on a diplomatic mission. The so-called king lost all real authority as punishment for summoning the Heroes without permission. The same goes for the crimson swine.”
“That sounds like a long and roundabout event.”
“And in the end, we’re basically just fools in this story.”
“The way you’re treating this like a game is a little concerning… but for now, it’s fine.”
“Once Father joins us, Ren and Itsuki should start to understand little by little.”
“Don’t you hate playing that kind of role?”
“Yeah.”
“Honestly, I’d rather just escape from this kingdom as soon as possible.”
Their distrust toward the kingdom was growing. Though it seemed they were still only half-convinced.
“I could tell you even more about the future, but I think we should focus on preventing this incident first. What do you think?”
“…Then let me ask you one last thing. Motoyasu, you used the phrase ‘the first world,’ didn’t you? You claim to have come from the future, but is this really the first time it’s happened?”
Oh? So he caught that. He was listening closely. I had said “the first world” without thinking, but it seemed to have worked in my favor.
“No, this isn’t my first time.”
“…I thought so.”

“There are multiple conditions that lead to my defeat. One of them is that if Ren, Itsuki, or Father dies, I get sent back to the day I was first summoned. There was even a time when Itsuki was killed by one of his own comrades.”
Hearing that he would be killed, Itsuki let out a startled cry. I nodded without hesitation. After all, I had seen it with my own eyes—Itsuki’s death.
“By those people?”
“I don’t know much about Itsuki’s party members, but a man in armor, who was originally in Ren’s group, ended up joining yours. And eventually, he turned against you.”
“I… see.”
“Is this really true? Honestly, I still can’t fully believe it… or rather, maybe I just don’t want to believe in a future like that.”
Is there something that could trigger Itsuki’s sense of justice and convince him? Let’s go through my memories…
Oh? There is something.
“Then how about we go confirm that this chainmail was stolen property? In the future, the evidence gets falsified, but right now, we should still be able to find proof.”
“It’s hard to say this isn’t just some elaborate scheme by the kingdom to make us believe Motoyasu, but…”
“That’s a bit of a stretch. Do you know how much effort it would take to summon us from another world just to put on an act?”
“…Yeah, you’re right.”
Well, it is a future where he gets killed. It’s only natural that he doesn’t want to believe it.
“Motoyasu, I’m sorry. I spoke out of turn.”

After Ren spoke, Itsuki nodded and then bowed his head to me. Itsuki—that arrogant Itsuki—actually bowed. Maybe he had been more humble in the beginning. In a way, he seemed more like a proper hero now than before.
“Alright. Let’s go see the proof that it was stolen.”
“Then we’ll head to the weapon shop you two visited today. That’s where Father bought it.”
“Understood.”
No time to waste. The shop might already be closed, but we should hurry.
“…I almost forgot, but how do you unlock the teleportation skill?”

“I’m in a ‘New Game Plus’ state thanks to my loops. The teleportation skill is attached to a weapon you obtain from the Dragon Hourglass’s sand. The condition for unlocking it is reaching a certain level.”
“I see… Not what I was hoping for, but still useful information in its own way.”

Well, if I dump too much information on them at once, Ren and Itsuki might reject it outright. That’s why it’s best to take things step by step—just like Father advised me in the previous loop. I’ll wait until they fully believe that I’ve come from the future before explaining the enhancement methods. Father also warned me not to make them think it’s just a game mechanic, like something that uses an NPC’s power.
